Let’s dive into Chapter 7: Deepening Relationships—Trust, Credibility, and Long-Term Value.
Once your solution lines up with what matters most to your organization, it’s time to focus on something even more important—strengthening your relationships with key stakeholders.
In the world of complex sales, trust and credibility are like currency. They’re what keep deals moving and partnerships thriving, especially when things get complicated or uncertain.
Here’s the thing—building trust doesn’t come from grand gestures. It’s really about showing up, over and over, with small but meaningful actions. Think of it like tending a campfire. You don’t just light it and walk away. You add a little fuel, shield it from the wind, and check on it to keep the flames steady.
So, how do you deepen those relationships in a practical way?
First, always follow through on your commitments, no matter how small they seem. If you say you’ll send over some info or check in next week, make sure you actually do it—and do it promptly.
Second, be honest about what you can and can’t deliver. If your solution won’t check every box, say so. People appreciate transparency, and working together to find alternatives shows you’re invested in their success—not just your own.
And don’t forget to share insights and resources that are truly useful, even if they don’t lead to a sale right away. When you become someone who helps just because you can, you quickly move from being just another seller to a trusted advisor.
Let me share a real-world example. Imagine a salesperson discovers that a client’s project is delayed because of budget cuts. Instead of pushing for a quick close, they offer to help the client build a stronger business case for next year’s budget cycle. That patience and support? It builds goodwill—and often, it leads to more opportunities down the road.
Trust also grows when you advocate for your client within your own company. Maybe they need a custom feature or special terms. When you take the time to champion their needs internally, clients notice. They see you working on their behalf, and their confidence in you grows.
Here are a few gentle reminders for nurturing trust:
Listen more than you speak. Let stakeholders share what’s on their minds.
Celebrate the small wins along the way—not just when the ink dries on a deal.
And stay engaged, even after the sale is done. Being present shows you care about their long-term success.
Over time, these habits build a strong foundation of credibility. They help you weather setbacks and open doors you might not have seen coming.
In complex sales, your relationships are your most valuable assets—they’re what drive long-term value and future growth.
